candidate_087.name: independent claim reanalysis with explicit inconclusive state and provenance-disjoint novelty gate
candidate_087.mechanism_hypothesis: Do not let an autonomous lab promote a material or mechanism claim directly from its own primary interpretation channel. Require an independent reanalysis or orthogonal confirmation channel for claim promotion; preserve an explicit inconclusive state when the available measurement cannot establish the claim; and separately verify novelty/provenance so training-set or platform-relative novelty cannot be reported as scientific novelty.

primary_evidence.source: Nathan J. Szymanski et al., Author Correction: An autonomous laboratory for the accelerated synthesis of inorganic materials, Nature 650, E1 (2026), published 2026-01-19, correcting the 2023 A-Lab article.
primary_evidence.naturalistic_reanalysis: After post-publication concerns about diffraction-based structure assignment, manual reanalysis confirmed 36 of 40 reported successes while 4 were judged inconclusive; the corrected success count excludes those four rather than forcing a binary success/failure label.
primary_evidence.provenance_boundary: The correction also clarifies that the original novelty language meant new to the prediction platform, not necessarily new to science, and removes Zn2Cr3FeO8 from the discussion because it had mistakenly been included in the training data.
primary_evidence.control_relevance: The episode gives unusually direct failure evidence for separating claim promotion from the same interpretation channel that generated the candidate, maintaining an inconclusive state under underdetermined characterization, and checking training/provenance identity before novelty claims are released.
primary_evidence.limits: This is a post-publication correction and peer-reviewed manual reanalysis, not a prospective randomized ablation of an autonomous validation gate. It therefore supports the guardrail target and failure mode, not a measured effect size for any specific automated gate implementation.

candidate_088.name: prediction-before-observation quantitative intent note plus orthogonal ambiguity resolution
candidate_088.mechanism_hypothesis: Before queuing a measurement, require the agent to record a quantitative expected signal, anticipated noise and an interpretation criterion; after acquisition, compare observation against that prediction rather than relying on narrative pattern recognition. If evidence is ambiguous, keep the interpretation provisional and allocate an orthogonal follow-up measurement rather than strengthening the claim through more verbal reasoning alone.

primary_evidence.source: Takuya Isogawa et al., Agentic AI for Scientific Reasoning in Autonomous Quantum Sensing Experiments, arXiv:2607.25145v1, submitted 2026-07-27.
primary_evidence.benchmark_design: The pODMR benchmark uses 96 archived measurements, three prompt conditions, GPT-5.4/GPT-5.5/GPT-5.6 Sol, four reasoning-effort settings and three replicate judgments per measurement, totaling 10,368 binary decisions. The expected-signal condition requires an explicit calculation or simulation before the resonance judgment and includes no labeled examples.
primary_evidence.quantitative_result: With pulse-sequence information alone, false-positive rates rose with reasoning effort: GPT-5.4 from 1.39% at low to 16.67% at xhigh, GPT-5.5 from 14.81% to 53.24%, and GPT-5.6 Sol from 26.85% to 45.37%. Requiring the expected-signal calculation kept false-positive rates between 0% and 3.70% across every model/reasoning combination.
primary_evidence.physical_workflow: In the autonomous NV-center workflow, the agent is instructed before measurement to record purpose, expected signal, anticipated noise and interpretation criteria. Ambiguous results remain provisional. In one live project it autonomously added a CPMG N=8 measurement to independently check a weak Ramsey feature, rather than relying on Ramsey alone.
primary_evidence.control_relevance: This is direct physical-science evidence that more reasoning is not monotonically safer for routine measurement interpretation and that a quantitative prediction gate can suppress optimistic false positives while still leaving hypothesis formation to the agent.
primary_evidence.limits: The false-positive comparison is offline on archived pODMR measurements, while only three end-to-end NV projects are reported. The expected-signal calculation was selected/written by the agent in the benchmark rather than always being an independently certified deterministic tool, so a live randomized controller comparison remains open.

candidate_089.name: formal executable-protocol compilation with staged semantic and hardware validation
candidate_089.mechanism_hypothesis: Treat natural-language experimental plans as untrusted source text. First classify them as executable, blueprint or incomplete; compile executable candidates into a formal machine-readable procedure; then require parser validity, source-to-protocol discrepancy checking and hardware-constrained simulation before physical execution. Feed only localized validation errors back for repair, and retrieve previously validated exemplars rather than arbitrary prior outputs.

primary_evidence.source: Sebastian Pagel, Michael Jirasek and Leroy Cronin, Verification and execution of the scientific literature via chemputation augmented by large language models, Communications Chemistry 9, 191 (2026), published 2026-04-03.
primary_evidence.validation_result: Across 150 randomly sampled ChemRnD procedures with at most six XDL-generation/validation iterations, 99.33% reached syntactically valid XDL but only 94.67% also passed procedure-XDL discrepancy checking and hardware-constrained execution simulation. This directly shows that syntax validity alone overstates readiness.
primary_evidence.admission_result: Among 717 extracted literature procedures, the system classified 427 as executable, 89 as blueprints and 201 as incomplete. Manual evaluation on 39 procedures yielded only 67.5% classification accuracy, with 75% of classification failures arising from ambiguous chemical references or general-procedure references, so the admission classifier itself remains a weak point that should not be treated as ground truth.
primary_evidence.memory_ablation: On 75 procedures, adding validated XDL examples, resolved ambiguities and external chemical data raised overall translation success from 85.3% to 93.3%. With all databases/external data removed, 98.7% still produced syntactically valid XDL but 14.7% failed later discrepancy/simulation stages.
primary_evidence.physical_scope: The paper reports six literature-derived syntheses executed on two robotic platforms; it also classifies one reported reaction as not reproducible without substantial alterations, demonstrating that validation can terminate in non-reproduction rather than forced execution.
primary_evidence.control_relevance: For autonomous-science agents, the useful pattern is not generic self-reflection but a promotion pipeline with explicit machine-checkable stages and a non-executable/incomplete state. Retrieval is most defensible when restricted to previously validated procedures and resolved ambiguities that are then rechecked against the current source and hardware.
primary_evidence.limits: The discrepancy critic is itself LLM-based, classification accuracy is modest, and the task is literature-to-protocol reproduction rather than open-ended discovery. The evidence supports staged validation and typed states, not fully autonomous scientific correctness.

candidate_078_threshold_check.result: The PhaseTransfer article was rechecked in full-text HTML. The acquisition switch is explicitly fixed at tau=0.6 in Eqs. 10 and 13, and no threshold-sensitivity experiment was surfaced in the article text. The paper says the qualitative switch behavior matters more than the specific functional form, but this is not evidence that tau=0.6 is robust or optimal. Keep tau sensitivity preregistered as unresolved.
